newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-Conseco buys distribution with deal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Conseco buys distribution with deal.

text.p: Conseco Inc agreed Wednesday to buy Leucadia National Corp's Colonial Penn Life Insurance Co in a move to gain a new channel for the distribution of its products.

The deal, which calls for Conseco to pay $460 million in cash and notes, will give the Carmel, Ind.-based financial services holding company an opportunity to cross-sell its current products using Colonial Penn's direct response marketing arm.
Conseco also reported $119.1 million in first-quarter operating profits that slightly exceeded Wall Street analysts' expectations, attributing them to sales and acquisitions.

Colonial Penn, probably best known for its television commercials featuring former "Tonight Show" sidekick Ed McMahon, sells life insurance to seniors using direct mail and telephone marketing in addition to the television ads.

Although Conseco has a broad distribution system, using both career and independent agents, Conseco chairman Stephen Hilbert said the company did not previously use direct marketing to sell its products.
"The one distribution point that we have been aggressively looking for is the right direct marketing company," Hilbert said.

"This is going to give us, again, an opportunity to hit the public and to target our markets as far as which segment of the buying public we want to target by the television ads and also the spokespeople that are delivering the message," he said.
Hilbert said he plans to sell Conseco's supplemental health, life, annuity and mutual fund products through Colonial Penn.
As a result, he said, he plans to allow Colonial Penn to continue operating the way it is in Philadelphia rather than consolidating it into Conseco and said he does not foresee much cost cutting.
The transaction is subject to customary terms and conditions, including regulatory approvals, and is expected to be completed in the third quarter of 1997, Conseco said.
The company said the transaction is expected to modestly increase operating profits in 1997 and 1998.
Conseco, one of the most acquisitive U.S. life insurance companies, said it will continue to look for additional acquisitions and has the financial flexibility to pursue deals as large as $2 billion.
The company also said it can use its equity to accomplish acquisitions or it can buy back about $1 billion of its own stock.
Conseco has completed 16 transactions involving more than 40 insurance companies since 1982.
The company's pending acquisition of Pioneer Financial Services is expected to close by the end of May.
"We've finished our rounding out with the Colonial Penn transaction," Hilbert said.
Conseco will look for acquisitions that will give it more critical mass in its chosen markets, he said.
Conseco's first quarter net income of $111.5 million more than doubled the $46.3 million it earned a year earlier.
The company earned 49 cents a share, up from 39 cents a share a year earlier, and revenue grew to $1.099 billion from $691.8 million.
The company had record operating earnings of $119.1 million, or 59 cents a share, versus $48.4 million, or 44 cents a share, a year earlier.
The First Call consensus operating earnings estimate was 58 cents a share.
